blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as powerful foundations for robotic manipulation, but their reliance on fixed camera configurations during training makes them brittle to changes in camera count or pose during deployment. To overcome these limitations, we propose VersaCamVLA, a camera-configurable framework that decouples camera-set representation from action learning. VersaCamVLA learns a unified scene-token interface that maps an arbitrary, variable set of posed RGB views into fixed-size latent scene tokens. This is achieved via multi-signal target-view prediction and Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling (WAPS), which leverages natural wrist-camera motion for free pose diversity. At deployment, a lightweight spatial encoder injects these compact scene tokens into a pretrained base VLA as a supplementary visual condition, requiring no explicit 3D sensing or novel-view rendering. Experiments on RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real-robot platform demonstrate that VersaCamVLA consistently outperforms prior VLA methods and direct multi-view baselines, maintaining robust performance across varying camera counts and unseen camera poses.
blocks.zh: Vision-Langage-Action(VLA)模型已作为机器人操控的强大基础出现,但它们在训练中依赖于固定的相机配置,使得它们在部署时难以改变相机计数或姿势. 为了克服这些局限性,我们提出VersaCamVLA,一个相机配置框架,将相机设定代表与动作学习脱钩. VersaCamVLA学习一个统一的场景切换界面,将一组任意,可变的RGB视图映射到固定大小的潜在场景符号中. 这是通过多信号靶景预测和Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling(WAPS)实现的,它们利用自然腕相机运动来自由摆放多样性. 在部署时,一个轻量级空间编码器将这些紧凑的场景符号注入一个预先训练的基座VLA,作为辅助视觉条件,不需要明确的3D感知或新视觉渲染. 在RoboTwin,LiBERO上的实验和一个真机器人平台显示,VersaCamVLA一贯优于先前的VLA方法和直接的多视基线,在不同的相机计数和看不见的相机姿势上保持强劲的性能.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have become a powerful foundation for robotic manipulation, adapting pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to map visual observations, language instructions, and proprioception to robot actions [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 ] , and their semantic priors and few-shot adaptability make them attractive as general policies across diverse tasks and environments.
However, fine-grained tasks such as precise insertion, and bimanual assembly demand reliable spatial perception, which is tightly coupled to the cameras used during training: changing the number of cameras or shifting a camera’s pose alters the visual token distribution and degrades the policy.
This poses a obstacle for deployment, where camera placement is often constrained by the robot, workspace, or task, and a useful view on one platform may be unavailable or suboptimal on another, as illustrated in Fig. 1 .
blocks.zh:
Vision-Langage-Action(VLA)模型成为了机器人操控的强大基础,将经过预先训练的Vision-Langage Models(VLMs)用于映射视觉观测,语言指令,以及机器人动作的自发性[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8],其语义学前科和几发相适应性使其具有吸引力,成为跨越不同任务和环境的一般政策.
然而,精细的任务,如精确的插入,以及双人组装,需要可靠的空间感知,这与训练时使用的相机紧密相接:改变相机数量或改变相机的姿势会改变视觉信号的分布并降低政策.
这给部署造成了障碍,因为相机的放置往往受到机器人、工作空间或任务的限制,一个平台上的有用视图可能不可用或另一个平台上的不理想,如图1所示。

blocks.en:
Prior work has addressed camera sensitivity through several complementary directions.
One line of work improves viewpoint robustness by collecting demonstrations from multiple camera poses [ 9 , 10 , 11 , 12 ] or synthesizing novel views for training-time augmentation [ 13 ] and training-free test-time adaptation [ 14 ] .
However, multi-pose collection is costly on real robots, and synthesis-based methods depend on the fidelity of generated views.
Another line introduces geometric priors through depth, point clouds, or rendered views [ 15 , 16 , 17 , 18 ] , as well as geometric features extracted from RGB images by pretrained 3D foundation models [ 19 , 20 ] .
Finally, multi-camera policies often append visual tokens from additional cameras to the policy input [ 21 , 22 , 23 ] .
This direct multi-view formulation improves coverage, but it still binds the policy to the camera count and view layout used during action learning, and its token length grows with the number of input views.
blocks.zh:
以前的工作通过几个互补方向解决了相机敏感性问题.
一行工作通过收集多相机显示的演示[9、10、11、12]或综合新观点用于培训时间增强[13]和无培训测试时间调整[14],提高了观点的稳健性。
然而,多pose收集对于真正的机器人来说成本很高,而以合成为基础的方法取决于所生成观点的忠实性.
另一行通过深度,点云,或使视图[15,16,17,18]引入几何前兆,以及由预先训练出3D基础模型从RGB图像中提取出几何特征[19,20].
最后,多相机政策常常将额外相机的可视标志附加到政策投入中[21、22、23]。
这种直接多视图的配制提高了覆盖范围,但它仍然将政策与动作学习中使用的相机计数和取景布局相接,它的符号长度随着输入视图的数量而增加.

blocks.en:
We argue that a VLA should instead support a camera-configurable visual pathway that accepts a variable number of posed RGB views, makes no assumption on camera poses, and presents the action policy with a unified fixed-size scene representation.
To this end, we present VersaCamVLA , a camera-configurable VLA framework that decouples camera-set representation learning from action learning.
Rather than redesigning the VLA backbone or requiring explicit 3D reconstruction, VersaCamVLA learns a unified scene-token interface between raw camera observations and the policy.
This interface maps any non-empty set of posed RGB views into fixed-size scene tokens, allowing different camera configurations to be represented through the same policy-facing visual format.

我们主张VLA应该支持一个相机可配置的可视化通道,接受可变数量的RGB观点,不假设相机的外观,并以统一的固定大小的场景表现来呈现动作政策.
为此,我们提出VersaCamVLA, 一个相机配置的VLA框架, 将相机设定的表达从动作学习中解开。
VersaCamVLA与其重新设计VLA主干线或要求明确的3D重建,不如在原始相机观测与政策之间学习统一的场景接地界面.
此界面将任何一组非空的 RGB 视图映射到固定大小的场景符号中, 允许不同的相机配置通过相同的外观格式来表示 。

blocks.en:
VersaCamVLA is trained in two stages: unified scene-token interface learning and scene-token-conditioned VLA policy learning.
In Stage I, a scene encoder aggregates a source set of posed RGB views into latent scene tokens, and a training-only scene decoder queries these tokens with target-camera rays predict RGB, semantic, and edge signals at target views.
This multi-signal target-view objective encourages the scene tokens to preserve view-consistent spatial information while providing object-level and boundary-aware supervision beyond raw pixel reconstruction.
To expose the encoder to diverse camera configurations without collecting additional multi-pose demonstrations, we introduce Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling (WAPS), which turns the natural motion of wrist cameras into a free source of pose diversity.
At each training frame, WAPS varies the source camera subset while asking the decoder to reconstruct all available views, producing both self-reconstruction and cross-view prediction signals for the same scene tokens.

blocks.en: In Stage II, VersaCamVLA discards the decoder and prediction heads, freezes the scene encoder, and integrates the learned scene tokens into a pretrained VLA policy. The base VLA keeps its native fixed-view RGB input and action-learning objective, while a lightweight spatial encoder compresses the learned scene tokens into a compact supplementary visual condition. Camera flexibility therefore enters through the auxiliary scene-token pathway: any available posed camera subset can be encoded into the same fixed-size representation, while the action expert receives a stable conditioning interface. At deployment, VersaCamVLA supports versatile camera setups and requires only RGB images with camera intrinsics and extrinsics. No novel-view rendering, depth estimation, point-cloud processing, or explicit 3D reconstruction is needed.

blocks.en:
We evaluate VersaCamVLA on RoboTwin [ 24 ] , LIBERO [ 25 ] , and a real-robot platform with varying camera counts and poses.
Across these scenarios, VersaCamVLA consistently outperforms prior works and direct multi-view baselines.
These findings show that learning a unified scene-token interface effectively makes pretrained VLA policies more robust to practical
camera-configuration changes.
In summary, our main contributions are threefold: • We formulate camera-configurable VLA policy learning, where a policy must operate with a variable number of posed RGB views without assuming fixed camera poses, while maintaining a fixed-size visual interface for action prediction. • We propose VersaCamVLA, a two-stage framework that learns a unified scene-token interface through target-view prediction,
then injects the resulting scene tokens into a pretrained VLA as supplementary visual conditioning. Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling is introduced to exploit wrist-camera motion as free pose diversity for scene-token learning. • We validate VersaCamVLA on simulation and real-robot manipulation benchmarks, showing consistent improvements over prior VLA methods and direct multi-view baselines under changing camera counts and unseen camera poses.

blocks.en: 2.1 Vision-Language-Action Models
blocks.zh: 2.1 远景-语言-行动模式

blocks.en:
Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 22 , 6 , 4 , 5 , 26 ] adapt pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to robot control by training on large-scale teleoperation and egocentric data, generalizing across novel scenes, objects, and instructions.
However, recent evaluations show that VLAs are sensitive to camera-configuration shifts, especially viewpoint variations [ 27 , 28 , 29 ] , mainly because their 2D RGB inputs lack explicit camera-pose awareness.
Most VLA policies further fix the number of input cameras during post-training, limiting adaptation to camera additions, removals, or pose changes.
Our work targets this underexplored camera-configuration flexibility for pretrained VLAs.

blocks.en: 2.2 Viewpoint Generalization for Vision-Language-Action Policies
blocks.zh: 2.2 展望-语言-行动政策概览

blocks.en:
Recent work addresses viewpoint brittleness in visuomotor and Vision-Language-Action policies through data augmentation, test-time view synthesis, and geometry-aware representation learning.
Data augmentation broadens viewpoint coverage through multi-pose demonstrations [ 9 , 10 , 12 ] or novel-view synthesis [ 30 , 31 ] , but is limited by collection cost and synthesis fidelity.
Geometry-aware methods inject priors such as depth [ 17 , 32 ] , point clouds [ 33 , 15 , 34 ] , or view-aligned 3D features [ 15 , 16 , 17 , 35 , 36 , 37 , 16 ] , as well as geometric features extracted from RGB images by pretrained 3D foundation models [ 19 , 20 ] .
In contrast, our method learns compact scene tokens from posed RGB views, improving unseen-pose robustness without explicit 3D reconstruction at deployment or extra multi-pose demonstrations, while requiring calibrated camera intrinsics and extrinsics.
blocks.zh:
最近的工作通过数据扩充、试验时间视图综合和几何-认识表现的学习,解决了图象运动和远景-语言-行动政策中的观点不清晰的问题。
数据增强通过多视角演示[9,10,12]或新颖视角综合[30,31]来拓宽视角覆盖面,但受收集成本和合成忠心度的限制.
几何感知法注入前名,如深度[17,32],点云[33,15,34],或取景相通的3D特征[15,16,17,35,36,37,16],以及由预修的3D基础模型从RGB图像中提取的几何特征[19,20].
反之,我们的方法从 RGB 的观点中吸取了紧凑的场景符号, 提高了隐形的坚固度, 而没有在部署时明确进行3D重建, 或额外多层的演示, 同时需要校正相机的内在和外观。

blocks.en: 2.3 Multi-Camera Perception for Vision-Language-Action Policies
blocks.zh: 2.3 愿景-语言-行动政策的多视角

blocks.en:
Multi-camera perception is a common strategy in imitation learning and robot manipulation.
Prior policies [ 21 , 22 ] concatenate image features or tokens from multiple cameras and feed them into a transformer-based action predictor.
Recent VLA-style approaches [ 38 , 22 , 23 , 39 , 40 , 41 , 42 , 43 ] adopt a similar design by appending external-view tokens to the policy input.
This direct multi-view formulation is simple and effective, and has been widely used to improve scene coverage, reduce occlusion, and enhance policy performance on fine-grained manipulation tasks.
blocks.zh:

先前的政策[21,22]从多相机中将图像特征或符号结合,并输入以变压器为基础的动作预测器.
最近VLA风格的方法[38, 22, 23, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43] 采用了类似的设计,将外部视图符号附在政策投入后.
这种直接的多景制式制作简单而有效,被广泛用于提高场景覆盖度,减少隐蔽性,并增强精细的操纵任务的政策性能.

blocks.en:
We present VersaCamVLA , a camera-configurable VLA framework that decouples camera-set representation learning from action learning, as illustrated in Fig. 2 .
In Stage I, VersaCamVLA learns a unified scene-token interface between raw observations and the policy. A scene encoder maps any non-empty set of posed RGB views to fixed-size latent scene tokens, supervised by target-view prediction, which encourages the scene tokens to preserve view-consistent spatial information across camera poses.
In Stage II, the decoder used for scene representation learning is removed, the scene encoder is frozen, and a compact version of the learned scene tokens is injected into a pretrained VLA policy as additional visual conditioning, allowing the policy to use observations from different numbers of cameras and unseen camera poses.

blocks.zh: 3.1 相机可配置VLA 设置

Standard VLA formulation. A VLA policy π \pi predicts robot actions at timestep t t from a language instruction ℒ \mathcal{L} , visual observation 𝒱 t \mathcal{V}_{t} , and proprioceptive state 𝒫 t \mathcal{P}_{t} , written as A t = π ⁡ ( ℒ , 𝒱 t , 𝒫 t ) = [ a t , a t + 1 , … , a t + H a − 1 ] , A_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{L},\mathcal{V}_{t},\mathcal{P}_{t})=[a_{t},a_{t+1},\ldots,a_{t+H_{a}-1}], (1) where H a H_{a} is the action horizon. Each action a t = [ 𝐪 t L , g t L , 𝐪 t R , g t R ] ∈ ℝ 14 a_{t}=[\mathbf{q}^{L}_{t},g^{L}_{t},\mathbf{q}^{R}_{t},g^{R}_{t}]\in\mathbb{R}^{14} is represented in joint space: 𝐪 t L , 𝐪 t R ∈ ℝ 6 \mathbf{q}^{L}_{t},\mathbf{q}^{R}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{6} are the left and right arm joint angles, and g t L , g t R ∈ ℝ g^{L}_{t},g^{R}_{t}\in\mathbb{R} are the gripper states.
In conventional single- or multi-view VLAs, 𝒱 t \mathcal{V}_{t} is tied to the camera setup used during policy training.
For example, a multi-camera VLA typically instantiates 𝒱 t \mathcal{V}_{t} as an image tuple { 𝐈 t i } i = 1 N \{\mathbf{I}_{t}^{i}\}_{i=1}^{N} , where the number of views and the camera poses are fixed components of the policy input.

Camera-configurable observations. The fixed-tuple visual observation in standard VLAs makes the policy interface depend on the demonstrated camera setup.
If a camera is added or moved to a new pose, the resulting visual tokens no longer match the structure seen during action learning.
To remove this dependency, we keep the standard VLA input-output form but replace the camera component of 𝒱 t \mathcal{V}_{t} with a flexible camera set.
Let 𝒞 = { ( 𝐊 i , 𝐓 i ) } i = 1 N \mathcal{C}=\{(\mathbf{K}^{i},\mathbf{T}^{i})\}_{i=1}^{N} denote a camera configuration, where 𝐊 i \mathbf{K}^{i} and 𝐓 i \mathbf{T}^{i} are the intrinsic and extrinsic matrices of camera i i .
Under this configuration, the visual observation is 𝒱 t 𝒞 = { ( 𝐈 t i , 𝐊 i , 𝐓 i ) } i = 1 N \mathcal{V}_{t}^{\mathcal{C}}=\{(\mathbf{I}_{t}^{i},\mathbf{K}^{i},\mathbf{T}^{i})\}_{i=1}^{N} .
Camera-configurable VLA policy learning asks for a single policy that remains valid as 𝒞 \mathcal{C} varies across deployment setups.
The visual observation should therefore allow a variable number of views from non-fixed poses, while the downstream action policy should still receive fixed-size scene tokens.
This motivates VersaCamVLA’s scene-token interface, which maps 𝒱 t 𝒞 \mathcal{V}_{t}^{\mathcal{C}} to unified scene tokens 𝐙 t \mathbf{Z}_{t} whose size is independent of N N .

blocks.en: 3.2 Unified Scene-Token Interface Learning
blocks.zh: 3.2 统一场景界面学习

blocks.en:
To implement a unified scene-token interface, VersaCamVLA uses a scene encoder that turns the camera-configurable observation into fixed-size scene tokens 𝐙 \mathbf{Z} .
Inspired by LVSM [ 46 ] , we learn this encoder with target-view prediction: a scene decoder , used only during representation learning, queries 𝐙 \mathbf{Z} with target-camera rays and reconstructs RGB, semantic, and edge signals.
This objective encourages 𝐙 \mathbf{Z} to support prediction at target views beyond the input views, while presenting the downstream VLA with a consistent visual representation regardless of the input camera set.

在LVSM[46]的启发下,我们用目标-视图预测来学习这个编码器:一个场景解码器,只在表现学习时使用,用目标-相机射线来询问Z\mathbf{Z},并重建了RGB,语义,和边缘信号.

blocks.en: 3.3 Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling
blocks.zh: 3.3 手推波斯取样

blocks.en:
The scene encoder in Sec. 3.2 is designed to accept a variable number of views from non-fixed poses and produce fixed-size unified scene tokens for downstream VLA.
Learning this camera-configurable interface, however, requires the training data to cover sufficiently diverse camera placements.
In tabletop manipulation data, static cameras provide stable but sparsely distributed viewpoints, while wrist cameras sweep a much richer pose distribution as the robot moves.
Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling (WAPS) turns this natural motion into pose diversity for scene-token learning.
blocks.zh:
Sec. 3.2中的场景编码器旨在接受从非固定姿势中得出的可变数量视图,并产生出下游VLA的固定大小的统一场景标志.
然而,学习这种相机配置接口需要培训数据,以涵盖足够多的相机配置。
在平面操纵数据中,静态相机提供稳定但分布稀少的视线,而手腕相机则会随着机器人的移动而扫取更丰富的姿势分布.
Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling (WAPS) 将这种自然运动变成了对场景学习的多元化.

blocks.en:
Specifically, for each training frame, let 𝒞 stat \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{stat}} and 𝒞 wrist \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{wrist}} denote the available static-camera and wrist-camera views.
The source view set 𝒮 = 𝒮 stat ∪ 𝒮 wrist \mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{stat}}\cup\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{wrist}} fed to the scene encoder is drawn from the two camera types independently.
From the static cameras, we randomly sample n n views as 𝒮 stat \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{stat}} , where n n is a random integer between 1 1 and | 𝒞 stat | |\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{stat}}| .
For wrist cameras, each view is independently included in 𝒮 wrist \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{wrist}} with probability 0.5 0.5 .
We use the full camera pool as the target set 𝒯 = 𝒞 stat ∪ 𝒞 wrist \mathcal{T}=\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{stat}}\cup\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{wrist}} , so the decoder is always trained to render every available view, regardless of the encoder input.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We present VersaCamVLA , a camera-configurable VLA framework that augments pretrained policies with a unified scene-token interface decoupling camera-set representation from action learning.
VersaCamVLA introduces a scene encoder learned by multi-signal target-view prediction and Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling that exploits wrist-camera motion as free pose diversity, producing compact scene tokens that condition a pretrained VLA without explicit 3D sensing.
Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and a real-robot platform show consistent improvements over prior VLAs and direct multi-view baselines under camera-pose perturbations and varying camera counts.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍VersaCamVLA,一个相机配置的VLA框架,它用一个统一的场景接地界面来强化预先训练的政策,从动作学习中解开相机设置的表示.
VersaCamVLA引入了由多信号目标-视野预测和Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling所学的场景编码器,该编码器利用了手腕-相机运动作为自由呈现出多样性,生成了紧凑的场景符号,将事先训练的VLA作为条件,而无需明确的3D感知.
在RoboTwin 2.0,LiBERO上的实验以及一个真机器人平台显示,在相机相机扰动和相机计数上,比之前的VLA和直取多视基线有一致的改进.

blocks.en:
Limitations and broader impacts. VersaCamVLA assumes calibrated camera intrinsics and extrinsics and focuses on tabletop bimanual setups with manual camera placement, lacking autonomous viewpoint selection.
Extending the scene-token interface to uncalibrated cameras, active perception that optimizes camera configurations online, and mobile workspaces remains key future work.
In terms of impact, we hope camera-configurable VLA policies lower the deployment barrier across robot platforms by reducing reliance on a fixed camera setup.
However, safety-critical deployment requires further validation against task-specific failures under large camera-configuration shifts.
blocks.zh:
限制和更广泛的影响。 VersaCamVLA假设了校正相机的内在和外显相机,并以手动相机放置的平面双人相机设置为重点,缺乏自主的视角选择.
将场景接地界面扩展至未校正相机,主动感知优化相机在线配置,移动工作空间仍然是未来的关键工作.
在撞击方面,我们希望相机可配置的VLA政策通过减少对固定相机设置的依赖来降低机器人平台的部署障碍.
然而,在大型相机配置转换中,对安全至关重要的部署需要进一步验证具体任务故障。

blocks.en: A.2 LIBERO

blocks.en:
We follow the standard LIBERO [ 25 ] protocol on a Franka Emika Panda arm in MuJoCo, with the four official task suites.
Our observation setup provides 6 environment cameras and 1 wrist-mounted camera per frame, forming the camera pool for Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling.
The four suites probe complementary capabilities, with LIBERO-Spatial evaluating spatial relationships among objects, LIBERO-Object testing generalization across object instances, LIBERO-Goal probing language-conditioned goal understanding, and LIBERO-Long covering long-horizon multi-step manipulation.

blocks.en:
VersaCamVLA uses camera extrinsics to encode the spatial relationships among input views, making calibration accuracy a practical consideration for deployment.

blocks.en:

blocks.en: C.1 Architecture Hyperparameters

blocks.en:
RGB observations are resized to 224 × 224 224\times 224 and tokenized with patch size p = 8 p=8 , yielding 28 × 28 = 784 28\times 28=784 patches per view.

Both the scene encoder Enc θ \mathrm{Enc}_{\theta} and the scene decoder Dec ψ \mathrm{Dec}_{\psi} are 12-layer Transformers with hidden dimension d = 768 d=768 , head dimension 64 64 (12 attention heads), QK-normalized attention, and depth-aware initialization for stable training.

blocks.en:
The spatial encoder is a lightweight convolutional module that maps the learned scene tokens to the token format expected by the base VLA policy.

This design provides a task-oriented bottleneck that preserves useful spatial cues while avoiding excessive token length during policy learning.

blocks.en: C.5 Camera-Pose Perturbation Sampling
blocks.zh: C.5 相机-波斯扰动取样

blocks.en:
At evaluation time, we perturb each camera by sampling its pose on a spherical shell centered on the workspace.
For each camera, we independently draw an azimuth offset Δ ​ ϕ ∼ 𝒰 ⁡ [ − 90 ∘ , 90 ∘ ] \Delta\phi\sim\mathcal{U}[-90^{\circ},90^{\circ}] , a radial scale r ∼ 𝒰 ⁡ [ 0.8 , 1.2 ] r\sim\mathcal{U}[0.8,1.2] that rescales the camera’s distance to the workspace, and a pitch θ ∼ 𝒰 ⁡ [ 25 ∘ , 75 ∘ ] \theta\sim\mathcal{U}[25^{\circ},75^{\circ}] ; the camera is then reoriented to look at the workspace center.
Camera configurations are resampled for each trial and shared between π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} and VersaCamVLA to ensure a matched comparison.
The stratified evaluation in Appendix B.3 restricts the absolute azimuth offset to the specified interval while retaining the remaining sampling settings.
